aiTitle: Connect to IPython notebook server from remote host

content.text:
Use an SSH tunnel from your local machine - no server config change needed.

```sh
# On YOUR machine (the one with the browser). Replace nick@server with the host running jupyter.
ssh -N -L 8888:127.0.0.1:8888 nick@<server-host>
```

Then open the same URL locally:
```
http://127.0.0.1:8888/lab/tree/docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb
```

Why this works: the server is bound to `127.0.0.1` (loopback), so it only accepts connections originating on the server itself. `-L 8888:127.0.0.1:8888` forwards your local port 8888 through the SSH connection to the server's loopback 8888, so from Jupyter's view the request still comes from localhost. The token in the URL stays valid because the host/port match.

Notes:
- If local port 8888 is taken, use `-L 9999:127.0.0.1:8888` and browse `http://127.0.0.1:9999/...`.
- Keep the `ssh -N` running; closing it drops the tunnel.
- Copy the full URL with `?token=...` from the `jupyter lab` startup log, or run `jupyter server list` on the server to get the token.

---

Alternative (only on a trusted/private network): bind the server to all interfaces and connect by IP.
```sh
jupyter lab --ip=0.0.0.0 --port=8888
# then from another host: http://<server-ip>:8888/lab/tree/docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb
```
This exposes the server to the network - the SSH tunnel is safer. Prefer the tunnel unless you have a specific reason.

aiTitle: Connect to IPython notebook server from remote host

content.text:
Set both the token and password to empty:

```sh
jupyter lab --ip=0.0.0.0 --port=8888 \
  --ServerApp.token='' --ServerApp.password=''
```

Key point: you must clear **both**. Setting only `token=''` still leaves Jupyter able to prompt; clearing both disables the login screen entirely, so the URL becomes just:
```
http://10.0.15.86:8888/lab/tree/docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb
```

Older config-key name (if your version complains): use `--NotebookApp.token='' --NotebookApp.password=''`.

Warning - this is a real exposure: with `--ip=0.0.0.0` and no token, anyone who can reach `10.0.15.86:8888` on your network gets full code execution as your user (Jupyter runs arbitrary shell). Only do this on a trusted LAN. The SSH tunnel keeps the token and avoids this.

`jupyterlab` still isn't installed in `/tmp/nbenv`. Want me to install it there and launch with the command above?
